title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (10-20Y nominal, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations — the UPDATED schedule sb0607 promised, masthead 'For Publication September 9, 2026', PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-15 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd — a DIFFERENT document from the 125,547-byte md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 August-5 schedule every prior assessment of this event read). The row reads verbatim announce 9/30/2026, operation 10/1/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 10/2/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 10Y to 20Y, maturity range 10/02/2036 - 10/01/2046, minimum purchase amount $0, maximum purchase amount '= or > $4 billion'. Stays estimate on two counts — the old third count, a SUPERSEDED $2B cap, is retired because that number is gone from the primary: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the maximum on this row is no longer a number at all, so the confirming primary is the 09-30 operation announcement (preliminary CUSIP list 11:00am ET on the announcement date per the schedule's own footnote 1). Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-15
notes: THE MAXIMUM ON THIS ROW IS NOT A NUMBER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The 2026-09-09 updated schedule prints '= or > $4 billion' for every long-end row it carries — 09-24, 10-01 (this), 10-08, 10-15, 10-27 and 11-04 — while every other sector keeps a printed figure (7Y-10Y 09-17 and 2Y-3Y 10-06 at $4 billion, 1Mo-2Y 11-05 at $4 billion, TIPS at $500 million / $750 million). So Treasury has stopped publishing a long-end maximum in advance; the announced maximum for this operation is genuinely unknowable until the 09-30 announcement. Press release sb0607 (2026-08-19) supplies only the floor, verbatim: Treasury is 'increasing, by at least double, the size of liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated nominal coupon securities (the 10-year to 20-year sector and the 20-year to 30-year sector). The current maximum size of $2 billion per operation will be at least $4 billion per operation. This change is effective September 9, 2026 and will be in effect for the remainder of this refunding quarter (through November 4, 2026).' The single precedent under the new regime says the floor is not the number: the 2026-09-10 10Y-20Y operation announced $6 billion (50% above the floor), drew $10.489B of offers (cover 1.75x) and accepted $5.187B — 86.4%, the sector's FIRST non-full fill in 26 operations — spread across 23 of 40 eligible issues against 1-5 issues in every prior 2026 operation in this bucket (api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations, 222 rows, pulled direct 2026-09-15, HTTP 200). Why it earns a slot: the calendar tracks the 09-10, 09-24, 10-08, 10-15 and 10-27 long-end operations inside sb0607's enlarged window and had skipped this one, leaving a gap in the series that matters most to treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09. It is also the first long-end operation of October and lands on the quarter-turn. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and a liquidity-support operation is a demand-side mechanic, not a price signal — the long end sold off THROUGH the first enlarged operation (10Y 4.784 on 09-04 to 5.010 on 09-15). Discovered during the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-06).
